scope: Actual stationary Diablo IV with external controlled pose samples, optical XY and scaled original pass depth. Successive partial views; no XR runtime.

summary.analysis: Mean-centered 49-sample local grayscale patches, downsampled 2x; fixed world ROI grid; acceptance only contrast/MAE/uniqueness, not expected motion. No full-scene guarantee.

wide_fov_observation: Visible missing/discontinuous regions; causes including original culling, unselected passes and screen-space dependencies remain unseparated.
limits: 26 accepted local terrain correspondences out of 45 contrasted patches do not establish whole-scene coverage.
Wide optical projection is currently a visible coverage failure, not a usable immersive result.
No actual XR pose/time or headset image in this game trial; two successive presents per pair.
Chosen metric scale and identity VIEW basis do not calibrate physical world size, gravity, tabletop placement or comfort.
No game D32 readback; source-depth mathematical/GPU preservation is proved separately with owned scenes.
Five registered queues with zero cross-queue camera waits do not certify arbitrary asynchronous game/runtime access.
CPU diagnostic exports and marker backpressure do not validate headtracking cadence.
Physical SteamVR DRM/WAW errors remain unresolved; native Windows D3D12/VR integration absent.
